rubric: Label changed Go functions review when their changed behavior affects access/tenant/object authorization, a disclosure boundary, executable capability or effect-ceiling enforcement, identity isolation, or directly asserts one of those invariants in a test (including extracted assertion helpers). Label generic plumbing, fixture setup, test doubles, pure serialization, effect accounting, evidence-integrity checks, and happy-path retry tests routine unless their changed behavior itself implements or asserts such a boundary. Supporting a security test or living in a security package alone is insufficient. Label unknown when the causal link cannot be resolved from pinned source and inspected caller context. Relevance is not a defect finding; routine is only out of scope for this authorization task and does not mean safe to omit from every review.
blinding: Read manifest and pinned git source/callers, plus previously fixed rubric only. No model predictions, selections, metrics, reports or other live reviewer judgments.
scope: Every changed Go function in supplied existing-open-PR snapshots. Non-function units excluded from this function relevance assessment; PR360 has no changed function units.
limitations: Existing open PR snapshots, not prospective future PRs.
Task relevance is not defect truth; potential correctness findings are separate and untested.
Functions correlated within PR; this cohort alone does not establish future population performance.
Focused source review, not exhaustive vulnerability analysis or runtime tests.

	return equalEffects(current.AdmittedEffects, wanted.AdmittedEffects) &&
		bytes.Equal(current.AdmittedDisclosures, wanted.AdmittedDisclosures) &&
		bytes.Equal(current.ID, wanted.ID) &&
		bytes.Equal(current.IdempotencyKey, wanted.IdempotencyKey) &&
		current.AgentID == wanted.AgentID &&
		current.AgentGeneration == wanted.AgentGeneration &&
		current.Capability == wanted.Capability &&
		current.Action == wanted.Action &&
		bytes.Equal(current.SourceID, wanted.SourceID) &&
		bytes.Equal(current.PolicyID, wanted.PolicyID) &&
		current.ObjectID == wanted.ObjectID &&
		bytes.Equal(current.Input, wanted.Input) &&
		current.Subject == wanted.Subject &&
		current.Actor == wanted.Actor &&
		current.ClientID == wanted.ClientID &&
		equalIDs(current.OnBehalfOf, wanted.OnBehalfOf) &&
		current.AuthorizationFingerprint == wanted.AuthorizationFingerprint &&
		current.PolicyGeneration == wanted.PolicyGeneration &&
		current.Reason == wanted.Reason &&
		current.Deadline.Equal(wanted.Deadline)

potential_defects.title: Egress-only admissions fail to mark a possible external effect
potential_defects.rationale: admitted sets EffectPossible only for EffectMutatesExternal, whereas ordinary DispatchService.Claim at this same head explicitly includes EffectEgressesContent. An admitted egress call can transmit and disappear while its claimed record says EffectPossible=false. The new test explicitly expects that false value. This is outcome-accounting correctness, separate from relevance to authorization.
potential_defects.trigger: Admit an action whose effects include egresses_content but not mutates_external, then perform egress without reporting.
potential_defects.validation: Static source contradiction only; no reproduction executed.

witnesses.relation: Existing claim contract explicitly charges possible egress

potential_defects.title: Outstanding admission list includes ordinary dispatch claims
potential_defects.rationale: Outstanding filters only claimed state, principal and current binding. Ordinary DispatchService.Claim creates the same state but leaves AdmittedEffects empty. Such work can appear as an outstanding admission despite never passing admission adjudication, confusing the operational picture. This is not evidence of a cross-principal leak.
potential_defects.trigger: Same principal enqueues and claims an ordinary dispatched action, then calls admission Outstanding.
potential_defects.validation: Static path inspection only; clarify whether deliberately treating every claim as an admission is intended.
